cards.explanation: The answer is Mary Magdalene. Mark says Jesus “…appeared first to Mary Magdalene…” (Mark 16:9). She's the one He had driven seven demons out of, and she's the first to see Him risen. I think that makes her morning pretty hard to top.
The answer is False. Mary sees Jesus, and then she goes and tells people. Mark 16:10 says, “She went and told those who had been with Him…” News like that has a way of leaving the building.

The answer is mourning. The people who had been with Jesus were “…mourning and weeping.” (Mark 16:10). So Mary is carrying the biggest news there is to people in tears. I think that's a hard moment to bring news into.
The answer is False. Mark 16:11 says, “…they did not believe it.” Mary tells them He's alive and that she has seen Him, and still they don't believe it. Not a quick yes anywhere in that verse.

The answer is True. Mark says Jesus “…appeared in a different form to two of them as they walked along in the country.” Mark doesn't tell us what that different form looked like, so I'm not going to make something up. I'll stick to what's in the verse, and it's plenty.

The answer is that they do not believe them either. Verse 13 says, “…they did not believe them either.” Jesus had appeared to two of His followers out in the country, and when those two report it to the rest, they get the same treatment Mary Magdalene got when she said she had seen Him alive. Two reports, and neither one is believed. That's a tough crowd, friends.

The answer is their unbelief and hardness of heart. Jesus “…rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart…” (Mark 16:14). Not fun to hear, and I've been scolded by a burnt tray myself. Still, notice that He appears to them while they're eating. He comes to the Eleven Himself.

The answer is those who had seen Him after He rose. Mark says the rebuke was “…because they did not believe those who had seen Him after He had risen.” That means people like Mary Magdalene and the two followers who met Him out in the country. The Eleven heard from eyewitnesses and didn't believe them.

The answer is world. Jesus says, “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.” That's a big territory, friends. I stay on one little planet and still struggle to cover it with cookies.

The answer is whoever believes and is baptized. Jesus says, “Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved…” (Mark 16:16). Two things go together there: believing and being baptized. Jesus just states it plainly.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “…whoever does not believe will be condemned.” (Mark 16:16). That's a heavy line, friends, and I won't joke about it. It's why this message matters so much.

The answer is driving out demons. That's number one on the list. Jesus says, “In My name they will drive out demons…” (Mark 16:17). Notice the words “In My name…” This one comes first, and the rest of the list follows.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will be made well.” (Mark 16:18). This one is a promise to believers, and Jesus says it plainly. It sits right there in His list of signs.

The answer is at the right hand of God. Mark says Jesus “…was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.” (Mark 16:19). That's where the story of Jesus' time with them ends. He is taken up, and then He sits down.

The answer is that they go out and preach everywhere. Mark says, “And they went out and preached everywhere…” (Mark 16:20). Jesus gave them the job, and they went and did it. The same group that hadn't believed the news is now out spreading it.

The answer is False. They do not go out without the Lord's help. Mark says, “…the Lord worked through them, confirming His word by the signs that accompanied it.” (Mark 16:20). They go out, and the Lord works through them. They aren't on their own.
